_meta.indication: Adjunct to diet and exercise to improve glycemic control in adults with type 2 diabetes mellitus

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study CV181011 (Study 11), a Phase 2/3 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled monotherapy trial
pivotal_trials.nct: Not stated in the reviewed documents
pivotal_trials.design: 24-week, double-blind, placebo-controlled monotherapy trial; after a 2-week single-blind diet, exercise, and placebo lead-in, patients were randomized to ONGLYZA 2.5 mg, 5 mg, or 10 mg or placebo
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with type 2 diabetes inadequately controlled on diet and exercise (A1C ≥7% to ≤10%)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Change from baseline in HbA1c at Week 24 (last observation carried forward before rescue)
pivotal_trials.n: 401 patients randomized (2.5 mg, 5 mg, 10 mg, or placebo)
pivotal_trials.result: At Week 24, placebo-corrected A1C change was -0.6% for both ONGLYZA 2.5 mg and 5 mg (2.5 mg 95% CI -0.9, -0.3; 5 mg 95% CI -0.9, -0.4), p<0.0001 vs placebo

nct_ctgov.title: Saxagliptin Treatment in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes Who Are Not Controlled With Diet and Exercise

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (≥5% and more common than placebo) were upper respiratory tract infection (7.7% vs 7.6%), urinary tract infection (6.8% vs 6.1%), and headache (6.5% vs 5.9%). Peripheral edema was more common with ONGLYZA 5 mg plus TZD (8.1% vs 4.3% placebo). Notable concerns included dose-related decreases in absolute lymphocyte count and hypoglycemia (add-on to glyburide 14.6% for 5 mg vs 10.1% placebo).
target_moa: Orally-active inhibitor of the dipeptidyl peptidase-4 (DPP4) enzyme; DPP4 inhibition increases active incretin hormones (GLP-1 and GIP), increasing glucose-dependent insulin secretion and decreasing glucagon

advisory_committee.vote: Presented before the Endocrine and Metabolic Advisory Committee on April 1, 2009. On CV safety the panel voted 10 yes, 2 no that saxagliptin ruled out unacceptable excess CV risk; and voted 0 yes, 12 no that postmarketing CV safety trials were unnecessary.

description.text: Revised Pediatric Use section based on pediatric study in type 2 diabetes patients ages 10 to <18 years

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sNDAs provide for revisions to section 8.4 *Pediatric Use* of the Onglyza and Kombiglyze XR Prescribing Information and Medication Guides based on the results of the pediatric study D1680C00019 (CV181375) entitled, A 26-week, *multicenter, randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, parallel group, phase 3 trial* with a 26-week safety extension period evaluating the safety and efficacy of *dapagliflozin 5 and 10 mg, and saxagliptin 2.5 and 5 mg in pediatric patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus who are between 10 and below 18 years of age*. Additional edits were made throughout the Prescribing Information and Medication Guides for Onglyza and Kombiglyze XR to modernize with current labeling guidances, clarify language, improve readability and organization of information, and align with other products.

basis.text: The application carried a Standard (S) priority designation, not Priority Review.

summary.text: Standard (non-priority) NDA for saxagliptin received June 30, 2008 and approved as a traditional (full) approval as an adjunct to diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes; an Endocrine and Metabolic Advisory Committee met April 1, 2009 focused on cardiovascular safety, and FDA required a postmarketing cardiovascular outcomes trial plus additional required postmarketing studies.

citations.quote: Please refer to your new drug application (NDA) dated and received on June 30, 2008, submitted under section 505(b) of the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act (FDCA) for Onglyza (saxagliptin) Tablets, 2.5 mg and 5 mg.
This NDA was presented before the Endocrine and Metabolic Advisory Committee on April 1, 2009.
